newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - Cosipa maintained as sell.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Cosipa maintained as sell.

text.p: -- ING Barings said in a report that it has maintained its sell rating on Brazilian steelmaker Cosipa as a result of worse-than-expected earnings for the company in the first quarter.
-- Analysts Mirela Rappaport said Cosipa posted a 28.4 million-real net loss in the first quarter of 1997 against ING's expectations of a 33 million-real net loss.
-- However, "excluding extraordinary items (the) bottom line was worse than our expectations," she wrote.
-- Cosipa sold 794,400 tonnes in the quarter, up two percent from 1996, while year-on-year domestic sales rose 26 percent to 482,800 tonnes, or 61 percent of total shipments, she added.
-- Higher domestic shipments, along with a better sales mix, led net revenues to rise to 317 million reais, up 12 percent yewar-on-year.
-- Despite efforts to improve operating performance and the overall better domestic market environment, Cosipa's results continued to be hurt by the firm's "extremely high interest expenses."
-- "Net interest expenses in the quarter accounted for 17 percent of total revenues," Rappaport wrote.
-- Cosipa's preferred B share was off 1.47 percent at 0.67 reais at 1657 local/1557 EDT in Sao Paulo while its common was untraded after closing May 14 at 0.55 reais.
